A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching core theory, algorithms, datasets, and experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original permutation experiments on 3,059 items, randomized support-dose outcomes, and a 528-item held-out audit, with additional results in the appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical studies and adds original model-breadth and permutation diagnostics in Appendix C.3 and Table 6.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same permutation sampling, Bernoulli KL budget, clipping, B2T calculation, and ISR >= 1 gate. The selective-classification framing and expanded deployment guidance do not specify a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same Factuality Slice coverage: FEVER, HotpotQA, NQ-Open, PopQA, and Controls. The added diagnostics extend Experiment 1 through model configurations and permutation procedures without introducing another dataset or evaluated task.

E2.justification: The uniform-mixture, optimized-mixture, and oracle single-permutation comparators remain unchanged in v2 Table 4 and v3 Table 5. The additional models are subjects of mechanism diagnostics; newly cited self-consistency and ensemble methods are not experimentally compared against ISR.

E3.justification: Appendix C.3 adds Llama-3.3-70B, gpt-4.1-mini, and DeepSeek-V3.2 configurations, logit-space slope and R-squared reporting, and a uniform-permutation condition for gpt-4.1-mini. This supplements the retained experimental protocols; the original studies' settings and Gemma fine-tuning parameters are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 adds focused checks of model breadth, whether logarithmic trends depend on banded permutations, and whether small probability-space slopes conceal logit-space sensitivity. The existing dose-response robustness checks and permutation-count/clipping sensitivity analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain Wilson intervals, OLS slope confidence intervals, fixed audit seeds, and the same significance-testing conventions. The new diagnostic table supplies point estimates without introducing additional run-count, uncertainty, or statistical-testing practices.

E6.justification: V3 Table 6 adds probability-space slopes of 0.0047 for Llama-3.3-70B, 0.0082/0.0049 for banded/uniform gpt-4.1-mini, and 0.0035 for DeepSeek-V3.2, plus logit slopes of 0.244 and 0.183 for the first two models. These are newly reported settings; the original experiment and appendix results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Proposition 3 and Appendix A.5 formalize ISR as a reject rule and provide a monotonicity argument for using q_lo conservatively when q_lo <= q_bar <= p*. The existing QMV, MDL, EDFL, rare-event, and clipping results and proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The three principal contributions and headline audit results remain. Section 1.2 narrows the causal claim from information itself to randomized support dose, while the abstract and conclusion more explicitly qualify the verifier-relative scope and the evidence from one audit.

C2.justification: V3 substantially revises interpretation and applicability: support dose is distinguished from the measured information-budget mediator; the audit is explicitly limited to one fine-tuned model; and verifier calibration and semantically ordered tasks receive concrete qualifications. Appendix C.3 adds a sigmoid-compression explanation for smaller probability-space slopes, and the discussion distinguishes ISR from generic ensembling.

D1.justification: The definite camera-ready code/data release promise becomes an unspecified statement about what a public release should include. Neither version supplies access links. Gemma fine-tuning details move from Section 4.1 to Appendix H.6 unchanged, rather than constituting new implementation disclosure.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning around rotary positional encodings and perturbation ensembling, adding works such as RoFormer, Barbero et al., Wang et al., and the Xu studies. It develops explicit distinctions from self-consistency and confidence-based selective prediction, while removing the earlier Su/Vasilatos lossy-compression discussion.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and closing discussion undergo substantial rewriting. Synthesis and Discussion are merged, impact material is relocated, operational explanations are expanded, Appendix C terminology changes, and author/affiliation and acknowledgement text is revised.

P2.justification: V3 converts the compact planner box into Table 1, adds diagnostic Table 6, relocates Figure 1, and revises captions and table placement. The existing plots and result-table structures largely persist; the worked example is also summarized from the retained appendix.

improvement.justification: V3 improves interpretive precision by identifying support dose as the randomized treatment and explicitly limiting the ISR evidence to a verifier-dependent, single-model audit. The added mechanism diagnostics and clearer exposition provide useful support. These gains outweigh the less definite release commitment, but remain limited by sparse reproduction details for the new diagnostics and the unchanged principal evidence.
